column8: Wed 18 Nov: store and evidence for row 23 (3e area 5): one of the best-known halls books 1-2 cents of doubt per pledged dollar in an ordinary year; excerpts of four years' statements; a recipient's books, never a co-sponsor's own.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 beside Q90-015: an arts hall's pledges sit on five names (65%), so a shortfall arrives as one name, not a percentage; supports row 28's unit; excerpts, a recipient's books.
Wed 18 Nov: store, evidence for rows 4 and 23; fix the use: 0.25% to 1.9% ($0.25M to $2.25M) is ninefold, not eightfold; the allowance is not split between building and other pledges.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 aha, losses come as names, not averages; compare on one base: the write-off was about 3% of all pledges at the year's start, twelve times the 0.25% allowance, and 4.4% is of building pledges only, so never set a quarter of a cent against 4.4 cents (use column, judge's note, best five #1).

Wed 18 Nov: 3d or 3e aha: a bank counted a hall's building pledges at 80-90 cents and still held collateral, the field that must lend against promises discounts them; stronger than Q22-023's bridge loan; a loan term, not a failure rate; the contribution is paid from Treasury funds she owns paying out in December 2032 (its day is not set, NUMBERS 8u).
Wed 18 Nov: store only; partners who share a donor share that donor's failure by a set ratio; two big institutions on one campus, no residency part needs it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e balance: most building pledges are paid, slowly, so the risk is a few lumps rather than a general fade; receivables also fall with write-offs and slower new pledges, so say paid down, never a collection rate.
Wed 18 Nov: store, the low end (73.6 cents) for row 23, almost all a time cut; its bridge financing repeats Q22-023; the RESIDENCY tag is loose (a museum wing).
Wed 18 Nov: store, evidence for row 23: a rich university at about 1 cent of doubt per pledged dollar; universities, not arts, beside Q53-020.

Wed 18 Nov: store beside Q53-022 and row 4: write-offs of 5.6% overran a reserve of about 3% by 1.8 times; row 4 makes the point for a building pledge, so this is the second instance, not a report line; arithmetic checks.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 yardstick, the plainest written rule found: a general reserve of 3 cents per pledged dollar plus specific reserves for late payers; one foundation's policy and a recipient's books.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 at most; S 3: the $48 million rests on press accounts of a return not read; the 40.6% sets a bad-debt line (not all of it pledges) against pledges and grants owed; the Kennedy Center is a recipient whose donors withdrew, not a co-sponsor's book; read the FY2025 990 before any use.
Wed 18 Nov: store beside row 12: the board's own slide says pledges fell more than 100% in four months after write-offs; a released internal document with no dollars, Keel reading.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5, a shortfall no market model sees (leadership, name, reputation); in the report dated facts only and no political cause named; fix the use: her flexibility is the money IPS l.15 names for a co-sponsor falling short, not sized (case l.106-107), a limit and not a promise, so never say it alone meets that loss.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d aha on owed against owned: one building campaign's fulfilment was 98% counted on track and 86% counted in hand; a pledge is owed, Laura's figure owned when she states it (IPS l.15); adds the two rates to H9-134.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5, a 2008-10 building case with its size: the lead donor delayed, half that year's promised gifts came, the province filled a $23 million gap (about 10.5% of $220M) with a loan; never give the lead pledge's size (30 or 23 million, conflicting); say can, never fall together.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, a pledge written on the donor's own investment is pencil, while Laura's top is stated only after the move into Treasuries (IPS l.15; l.16 is blank); a true fact behind 3d's ink, not a second turn (CONCEIT V2.2); say his investment in a hotel; the condition is his lawyer's account; adds an explicit condition to H7-070.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 and beside aha 8: in a building campaign about 70% is still a promise when the asking stops, and redemption follows the project; one consultant's experience, not a survey.
Wed 18 Nov: store, the source of the planning 10% in row 27; practitioners' advice read as an excerpt, not data.
Wed 18 Nov: store guard: never quote vendors' 10-30%, a church lender's 20-50% haircuts or the misquoted Urban Institute 6-9%; use audited statements and Q53-021's survey.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e wording: building pledges run longer, so more are open when a downturn or a delay comes; never fail twice as often; cases, not a sample.

Wed 18 Nov: store; a recipient's doubt depends on its donors as much as on the economy (Carnegie lowest in 2021, Fox Cities none in 2010, ASU 30.7%), so no yardstick carries from one institution to another.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5's one sentence, with three fixes: these are recipients' books, never co-sponsors' own (Q90-008's fix); Lincoln's 4.4% is of building pledges, about 3% of all; the Kennedy two-fifths rests on press accounts of a return not read (S 3), so leave it out until the FY2025 990 is read.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3e area 5 Taiwan: say the rule has no article on pledges, not that the books have no pledge rule (art. 2 sends gaps to general standards); read on a mirror, check the official text before citing.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 client knowledge for Taiwan: the largest private building gift came built, in kind, and its equipment money stayed verbal for years until a contract; adds the in-kind form and the verbal stage to Q52-026; never imply her flexibility covers a gap of that size.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5 Taiwan, Keel inference on few cases: a shortfall is more likely through a figure never written down than a written pledge unpaid, which 3d's written ask answers; never close date in Laura's own words (voice round 8).

Wed 18 Nov: 3b illustration only (case l.106-107, CANON A31); figures check against NUMBERS 8o (18.4%, 24.9%) and the sources; drop the Kennedy-like 41% until its return is read (S 3); say both parts of her flexibility; a limit, not a promise; row 28's one-name unit is the honest frame, so the percentages stay in the store.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b, gives a co-sponsor falling short a size from the register; arithmetic checks (21,179 and 28,682 over 115,000 are 18.4% and 24.9%, NUMBERS 8o, 8u); say about $21,200, not $21,000 (WORDS), and about 25% on today's figures, never a quarter (WORDS keeps about a quarter for 26.1%); measured on 1 Jan 2033; could stand in for, never sized for.

Wed 18 Nov: store only, scale for the lead's checks; arithmetic checks against NUMBERS 8o (about $212,000, $287,000, $69,000, $93,000, $96,000, $162,000); never a figure for what co-sponsors will pledge or the funding gap (case l.164-166).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area 5, one clause beside aha 9: shares flat to the move then 40% down leave her flexibility $8,852, or $17,427 with anything above the top (NUMBERS 8p checks; 8.0% and 15.8% of $110,000); co-sponsors can fail in the same downturn, never fall together; ASU's is a recipient's estimate.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b guard, one pool for the three uses, never added up as separate pots; $28,682 less $11,500 is $17,182, about 15% of $115,000 (NUMBERS 8j, 8o check); name the $28,682 as her flexibility ($21,179) plus anything above the top ($7,503), never under the name alone (WORDS); the subtraction ranks no use.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3: a pledge fails on its payment date, so the third use can come after 1 Jan 2033, the date NUMBERS measures her flexibility; name that date; say nothing on how it is held after 2033 (not in the IPS).
